question: Since 1 January 2025, under Article 11(1) of Directive 2008/98/EC on waste, as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/851, Member States have been required to use separate collection systems for textile waste. There are still significant problems in Sicily regarding the collection and management of used textiles.

Sicily’s regional waste management plan highlights the need to improve separate collection, increase the number of drop-off points, and develop the textile reuse and recycling chain. These issues risk undermining the effective implementation of Article 11 of Directive 2008/98/EC and the objectives of the circular economy. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission believe that the textile waste management problems in Sicily are compatible with the requirements laid down in Article 11 of Directive 2008/98/EC?

Will it verify whether Italy has put in place all the necessary measures – including adequate collection and treatment capacities – to ensure that Directive 2008/98/EC is properly implemented throughout Italy?

What steps will it take to support Member States and regions with inadequate textile waste management capacities to ensure that they comply with EU legislation and achieve the objectives of the circular economy?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.10.2026) Article 11(1) of the Waste Framework Directive (WFD)1 requires Member States to set up separate collection for textiles by 1 January 2025.

The organisation and enforcement of waste collection and treatment systems fall primarily within the competence of Member States and, where relevant, of their regional and local authorities, including as regards to which textiles are covered by the separate collection system.

Therefore, it is for the Italian competent authorities to ensure that textile waste in Sicily is collected and treated in compliance with EU waste legislation. To support Member States in managing used textiles and textile waste, Directive (EU) 2025/1892 recently amended the WFD and introduced mandatory national extended producer responsibility (EPR) obligations for textiles.

Under the revised rules, producers2 falling within the scope of EPR obligations will have to bear the costs of collecting used textiles and textile waste, and their subsequent treatment (Article 22a(8) of the WFD). Member States must transpose Directive (EU) 2025/1892 by 17 June 2027 and put the EPR obligations in place by 17 April 2028.
The Commission may assess compliance with the WFD based on sufficiently substantiated information indicating structural or persistent breaches.
1 Directive 2008/98/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 November 2008 on waste and

repealing certain Directives, OJ L 312, 22.11.2008, p. 3–30, as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/851 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 30 May, OJ L 150, 14.6.2018, p. 109–140 and Directive (EU) 2025/1892 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 September 2025, OJ L, 2025/1892, 26.9.2025. 2 Article 3(4b) of the WFD.
